claim: States the four metric-space axioms (non-negativity, identity of indiscernibles, symmetry, triangle inequality) that the Kendall-Tau distance satisfies.
equation: \left\{ \begin{array}{cc} d(i, j) \geq 0 & \text{(Non-negativity)}\\ d(i, j)=0 \Leftrightarrow i = j & \text{(Identity of Indiscernibles)}\\ d(i, j) = d(j, i) & \text{ (Symmetry)}\\ d(i, j) + d(j, k) \leq d(i, k) & \text{ (Triangle Inequality)} \end{array} \right.

claim: States the metric-tree partition invariant: every object in the Inner set is strictly closer to the root than every object in the Outer set.
equation: \forall i \in Inner, \forall j \in Outer;\:d(root, i)<d(root, j)

claim: Defines r_min as the minimum distance from the root object to any object in the set.
Defines r_max as the maximum distance from the root object to any object in the set.
Defines r_inner as the maximum distance from the root to any object in the Inner set.
Defines r_outer as the minimum distance from the root to any object in the Outer set.
Metric-tree query condition 0: the root object lies within the query ball of radius r_q around query object q, so it is added to the answer set.
Metric-tree query condition 1: the query ball lies entirely inside the minimum boundary r_min, so the branch is pruned.
Metric-tree query condition 2: the query ball lies entirely outside the maximum boundary r_max, so the branch is pruned.
Metric-tree query condition 3: the query ball intersects the Inner (left) subtree boundary r_inner, so the left subtree is searched.
Metric-tree query condition 4: the query ball intersects the Outer (right) subtree boundary r_outer, so the right subtree is searched.
Defines the ball query: the answer set A contains every object a whose distance to the query object q is at most r.
Defines the ring query: the answer set B contains every object b whose distance to the query object q lies between r_minq and r_maxq.
equation: \forall b \in B\; r_{minq}\leq d(b, q)\leq r_{maxq}
